raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week plan summary for your beginner client training in a small flat with a doorway pull-up bar and yoga mat. It includes the strength program (3 days/week), cardio (2–3 days/week), Saturday finisher options, mobility routine, nutrition, and Phase 2 intensity push. Use Mon/Wed/Fri for strength, Tue/Thu for cardio or mobility, Sat finisher, Sun recovery.

Program structure at a glance
- Training frequency: 3 strength days/week (A/B full-body), optional 2–3 cardio sessions/week, Saturday finisher (fun), daily short mobility.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundations and capacity
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification (pushed harder as requested)
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and performance
- Session length: 45–60 minutes (main days). Finishers and cardio: 20–30 minutes. Mobility: 8–15 minutes.
- Progression: Reps → tempo/pauses → leverage → density/EMOMs → small external load (backpack) as needed.
- Rest: 60–120s accessories; 90–180s primary lifts; longer in Phase 2 heavy days.

Weekly template
- Mon: Strength Session A
- Tue: Cardio (Zone 2 or intervals) + mobility
- Wed: Strength Session B
- Thu: Cardio (Zone 2) or mobility-only if fatigued
- Fri: Strength Session A/B alternating by week
- Sat: Fun Finisher Day (rotate themes)
- Sun: Recovery walk + full mobility

Warm-up (every strength session, 5–8 min)
- 2–3 min light cardio (march or shadowbox), cat–cow x5, T-spine rotations, hip circles, ankle rocks
- Activation circuit x2: 8 scapular pull-ups or depressions, 10 glute bridges, 10 dead bugs/side, 20s high plank

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundations
- Goal: Groove technique, build volume, core and scapular control.

Week 1
- Session A
  1) Incline push-up 4x8–10 (3010)
  2) Assisted pull-up 4x5 (31X1) + 1–2 slow eccentrics
  3) Bodyweight squat 4x12 (3011; 2s pause last rep)
  4) Glute bridge 3x12–15 (21X1)
  5) Hollow tuck hold 4x20–30s
  6) Side plank 3x20–30s/side
- Session B
  1) Knee/incline push-up 4x10–12
  2) Inverted/towel row 4x8–10 (2111)
  3) Split squat 3x8–10/leg (3011)
  4) Hamstring sliders 3x6–8
  5) Dead bug 3x8–10/side
  6) Wall slides or prone Y-T 3x10–12
- Micros (optional): 2x/week easy scap pulls 5 reps + hollow 20s

Week 2
- Session A: Progress reps/angle on push-ups; assisted pull-ups 5x5 + 2–3 eccentrics; tempo squat 4x12; single-leg glute bridge 3x10–12; hollow one-leg extended 4x20–30s; side plank with top-leg abduction
- Session B: Regular push-ups (if 8+ reps) or lower incline; rows 4x10–12; split squats 4x10/leg; sliders 4x6–8; dead bug 3x10–12; pike scap shrugs 3x10–12
- Micros: GTG assisted pull-up singles 4–6 total

Week 3
- Session A: Push-up 4x8–10 (feet slightly elevated if strong); assisted pull-up 5x6 + 2–3 eccentrics; pause squat 4x10 (2s); couch hip thrust 3x12–15; hollow rock (tuck) 4x15–20; side plank 3x30–40s
- Session B: Narrow push-up 4x8–10; row 4x10–12 with 2s top hold; reverse lunge 4x10/leg; sliders 4x8–10; dead bug heel taps; prone swimmers
- Micros: Mobility 10–12 min + 3x20–30s active hang

Week 4 (Deload/technique)
- Session A: Push-up 3x6–8; assisted pull-up 3x4–5 + 1–2 eccentrics; squat 3x10; glute bridge 3x12; hollow 3x20s
- Session B: Push-up 3x6–8; row 3x8–10; split squat 3x8/leg; sliders 3x6; side plank 3x20–30s
- Micros: Off or light

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification (pushed)
- Global: Top sets 4–6 reps @ RPE 8–9; clusters; 4–5s eccentrics; 2–3s pauses; longer rests; keep Week 8 as a lighter reload but higher than Phase 1 deload.

Week 5
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up: Top set 6RM; 2 back-offs x6 at ~90% with 41X1
  2) Pull-ups: Singles/doubles to 6–8 total strict/assisted; 2x8–10s eccentrics
  3) Bulgarian split squat 4x6–8/leg (3s pause)
  4) Single-leg hip thrust 3x8–10/leg
  5) Hollow hold 4x30–35s
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up: Top set 5–6 @ RPE 9; then 3x4–5 (31X1)
  2) Row 5x6–8 (2–3s top hold, harder angle/backpack)
  3) Tempo squat 4x8–10 (31X1; 3s pause last rep)
  4) Sliders 3x10–12
  5) RKC plank 4x20s
- Micros: One 8–10 min push-up EMOM (5 reps hard variation); 6–8 easy pull-up singles across 2 days

Week 6
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated/weighted push-up clusters: 4 clusters of 2-2-2 (20–30s between mini-sets)
  2) Pull-ups: 5–7 strict singles; fill to 10 reps total with minimal-assist doubles; 2x8–10s eccentrics
  3) Bulgarian split squat 5x6/leg (31X1) + 10s iso hold after last rep
  4) Single-leg hinge pattern 3x10/leg
  5) Hollow rock 4x20
- Session B
  1) Elevated pike or pseudo-planche lean push-up 5x4–6 @ RPE 8–9
  2) Heavy rows 5x6–8 (3s eccentric)
  3) Reverse lunge 4x8/leg (2s pause)
  4) Sliders 4x10–12
  5) Side plank reach-through 3x30s/side
- Micros: GTG pull-up singles 6–10 total; 6-min push-up EMOM once (4–6 hard reps)

Week 7
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated/weighted push-up 6x4–5 @ RPE 9 (41X1)
  2) Pull-ups: Attempt 1–3 strict singles; then 4x2 cluster (1-1 with 20s) assisted; 1–2 eccentrics 10s
  3) Bulgarian split squat 5x6–8/leg (3s pause); last set AMRAP-1
  4) Single-leg hip thrust 3x10/leg
  5) Hollow hold 4x35–40s
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up 6x4–5 heavy; elevate feet if needed
  2) Row 6x5–6 (3s top hold); final set AMRAP-1
  3) Tempo squat 4x8 (31X1)
  4) Sliders 4x12
  5) Hanging knee/tuck raises 4x6–8
- Micros: Optional easy singles only; skip density if joints are cranky

Week 8 (Reload)
- Session A: Feet-elevated push-up 3x5–6 @ RPE ~7; pull-ups 5x1–2 technique + 1x8s eccentric; Bulgarians 3x6–8; sliders 3x10; hollow 3x25–30s
- Session B: Pike push-up 3x4–6; row 3x8; squat 3x8–10; glute bridge 3x12; side plank 3x20–30s

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and performance
- Goal: Cement full pull-ups, push strength, unilateral legs; add density tests smartly.

Week 9
- Session A: Feet-elevated or backpack push-up 5x5–7 (31X1); pull-up ladder 6–8 total strict reps + 2 eccentrics; Bulgarians 5x8/leg (2s pause); single-leg hip thrust 4x10; hollow 4x30–40s
- Session B: Pike push-up 5x5–7; row 5x6–8 (3s top hold); tempo squat 4x12; sliders 4x10–12; hanging knee raises 4x6–10

Week 10
- Session A: Push-up density EMOM 10 min x 5–7 feet-elevated reps; pull-ups 6–10 strict total reps (fill to 15 vertical pulls w/ assistance); Bulgarians 4x10/leg (last set AMRAP-1); hollow rock 4x20–30
- Session B: Pike push-up 5x6–8 or elevated pike; row 4x8–10 (add backpack if needed); assisted Cossack 3x6–8/side; sliders 4x12; RKC plank 5x20s

Week 11
- Session A: Weighted backpack or higher-elevation push-up 5x5–6 (31X1); pull-ups 8–12 total reps (cluster 1-1-1 with short rests) + 1–2 eccentrics; Bulgarians 5x8/leg (31X1) + 10s iso; hanging knee raise 4x8–10; side plank 3x30–40s
- Session B: Pike push-up 5x6–8; row 5x6–8 (2–3s hold); assisted shrimp squat 4x4–6/leg (31X1); sliders 4x10–12; hollow 4x30–40s

Week 12 (Test/consolidate)
- Session A (Upper test): Max strict push-ups (or at set elevation) to clean-form limit; Pull-up test—max strict singles with 60–90s rest; if assisted, count quality 5–8s eccentrics; Accessories easy: Bulgarians 2x8/leg, hollow 2x20s
- Session B (Lower/core): Bulgarians 4x10/leg; sliders 4x10–12; hanging knee raises 4x8–10 slow; pike push-up 3x6–8 easy

Cardio plan (at home, 2–3x/week, 15–30 min)
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): 2x/week, easy/moderate
  - Options: 15–25 min steady march + shadowbox; or 6–10 rounds 45s step-ups + 30–45s easy; or 4–5 rounds aerobic flow (5 min/round)
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Keep 1 Zone 2 session; add structured intervals
  - Session 1: 22–26 min continuous Zone 2
  - Session 2: 8–10 rounds 40s hard + 50–60s easy (step-ups, fast march, shadowbox)
  - Optional Session 3: Ladder intervals 2–3–2 min moderate-hard with 2 min easy between
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): 2–3x/week
  - Session 1: 25–30 min Zone 2
  - Session 2: 8–10 rounds 30–40s hard + 60–75s easy
  - Session 3: 20-min EMOM mixer (step-ups, shadowboxing, high-knee march, mobility)

Saturday “Fun Finisher” (pick one each week, 20–30 min)
- Pull-up Party + Core: Ladder 1–2–3–2–1; hanging core medley; 6-min EMOM with pull-up singles + plank taps
- Push-up Gauntlet: 3 mechanical drop-set rounds; E2MOM skill block (supports, scap pulls, rows); hollow rocks
- Lower-Body Burner: 4–5 rounds of Bulgarians, hamstring sliders, lateral step-backs; 5-min “stairs without stairs”
- Shadowbox + Steps: 8 rounds of 2-min work (alternating shadowbox/step-ups) + 1-min easy; core wrap
- EMOM Mixer (20 min): M1 pull-ups, M2 push-ups, M3 step-ups, M4 hollow + slow climbers
- 15-min AMRAP “3-6-9-20s”: 3 pull-ups, 6 push-ups, 9 squats, 20s hollow; beat last score

Mobility routine (daily 8–15 min; mini 5–7 min pre-lift)
- Flow: Crocodile breathing → cat–cow + thread-the-needle → wall/floor angels → scap pulls + active hang → hip flexor half-kneel → 90/90 switches → hamstring strap stretch → adductor rocks → ankle knee-to-wall → doorway pec stretch → shoulder extension on couch
- Mini warm-up pre-lift: March 30s, arm circles, cat–cow x5, World’s Greatest x2/side, scap pulls x6 + active hang 20s, 10 pause squats, 20s plank
- Post-session cooldown: 90/90 breathing, hip flexor and pec stretch

Nutrition plan (12 weeks, habit-based with macros)
- Calories: Maintenance to slight surplus (+150–300 kcal/day) to drive strength; adjust weekly by scale trend (+0.1–0.25% BW/week)
- Protein: 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day (evenly across 3–5 meals)

Equipment roadmap (apartment-friendly)

- Pull: Several strict singles or strong assisted sets with long eccentrics; better scapular control and hang tolerance

Here’s a structured 12-week strength program designed for a beginner training in a small flat with only a doorway pull-up bar and a yoga mat. It focuses on full-body strength with progressive overload using bodyweight variations, tempo, pause work, and density progression. It’s split into 3 phases to build fundamentals, then intensify, then consolidate and test. Sessions target 3 days/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) with optional short “micro-sessions” on two additional days for skill/grease-the-groove. Each main session is ~45–60 minutes.

Guiding principles
- Progression: Increase difficulty by reps, sets, tempo, leverage (harder angles), pauses, and reduced rest.
- Technique first: Maintain controlled eccentrics, full range of motion, bracing, and scapular control.
- Warm-up every session: 5–8 minutes mobility + activation.
- Rest between sets: 60–120s for accessories; 90–150s for main strength moves.
- Logging: Track reps completed, RPE (aim RPE 7–9 on final set), and form quality.

Key movements and progressions
- Push: Incline/regular push-ups → feet-elevated push-ups → pseudo planche lean push-ups.
- Pull: Inverted row (using bar in low position if possible) or towel rows under bar → assisted pull-ups (chair/leg assist) → controlled eccentrics → full pull-ups → archer/weighted backpack options.
- Squat/hinge: Bodyweight squat → tempo/pause → narrow/Cossack progression → split squat → Bulgarian split squat → shrimp squat (assisted).
- Posterior chain: Hip hinge via sliding hamstring curls (towel on floor), glute bridge/hip thrust, single-leg variations.
- Core/bracing: Hollow body progressions, dead bug, side plank, RKC plank, hanging knee raise progressions.
- Scapular/shoulder: Scapular pull-ups, wall slides, reverse snow angels, pike shoulder taps.

Weekly structure
- Main days (3x/week): Full-body A/B rotating across weeks.
- Optional micro-sessions (2x/week, 10–15 min): Easy technique sets of pull-ups/rows, hollow holds, mobility.

Warm-up template (every session)
- 2–3 minutes light cardio (march in place, jumping jacks if neighbors allow).
- Mobility: neck nods, T-spine rotations, cat-cow, hip circles, ankle rocks.
- Activation circuit x2: 8 scapular pull-ups or bandless scapular depressions hanging from bar, 10 glute bridges, 10 dead bugs per side, 20s high plank.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundations and capacity. Learn positions, accumulate quality volume.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification. Harder leverage, eccentrics/pauses, lower reps, longer rests.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and performance. Progress to full pull-ups, feet-elevated pushes, unilateral legs, and density/EMOM tests.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundations)
Goal: Groove technique, build joint tolerance, core/bracing, scapular control. Progress by reps then leverage.

Week 1
- Session A
  1) Incline push-up (hands on desk/counter) 4x8–10, 3010 tempo
  2) Assisted pull-up (one foot on chair, minimal assist) 4x5, 31X1 tempo; finish with 1–2 controlled 5–8s eccentrics
  3) Bodyweight squat 4x12, 3011; last rep 2s pause
  4) Glute bridge 3x12–15, 21X1
  5) Hollow body tuck hold 4x20–30s
  6) Side plank 3x20–30s/side
- Session B
  1) Knee or incline push-up 4x10–12, 2011
  2) Inverted row variation: Set bar low in doorway if safe; if not, towel row seated under bar (heels down, pull chest to bar) 4x8–10, 2111
  3) Split squat (rear foot on floor) 3x8–10/leg, 3011
  4) Hamstring sliders (towel under heels, hips up) 3x6–8
  5) Dead bug 3x8–10/side with slow exhale
  6) Scapular wall slide or prone Y-T raise on floor 3x10–12
- Optional micro-sessions (2x): 5 sets easy scapular pull-ups 5 reps + hollow hold 20s + ankle/hip mobility.

Week 2
- Session A
  1) Incline push-up 4x10–12, 3010
  2) Assisted pull-up 5x5; add 2–3 eccentrics (6–8s)
  3) Tempo squat 4x12, 31X1, 2s pause last rep
  4) Single-leg glute bridge 3x10–12/leg
  5) Hollow body hold (tuck-to-one-leg-extended) 4x20–30s
  6) Side plank with top-leg abduction 3x15–20s/side
- Session B
  1) Regular push-up (if 8 quality reps) or lower incline 4x8–10, 2111
  2) Towel/inverted row 4x10–12
  3) Split squat 4x10/leg, 3011
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x6–8
  5) Dead bug 3x10–12/side
  6) Pike scapular shrugs 3x10–12
- Micros: Grease-the-groove (GTG) assisted pull-ups 4–6 singles, very easy.

Week 3
- Session A
  1) Push-up 4x8–10, 3010; elevate feet slightly if 12+ easy
  2) Assisted pull-up 5x6; finish with 2–3 eccentrics 6–8s
  3) Pause squat 4x10 (2s at bottom)
  4) Hip thrust feet on couch 3x12–15
  5) Hollow rock (tuck) 4x15–20 rocks
  6) Side plank 3x30–40s/side
- Session B
  1) Narrow-grip push-up 4x8–10
  2) Inverted/towel row 4x10–12 with 2s hold at top
  3) Walking reverse lunge (in place) 4x10/leg
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x8–10
  5) Dead bug with heel tap 3x12/side
  6) Prone swimmers 3x10
- Micros: 10–12 minutes mobility; 3x20–30s active hang.

Week 4 (deload/technique consolidation)
- Session A
  1) Push-up 3x6–8, 2111
  2) Assisted pull-up 3x4–5, crisp; 1–2 eccentrics 5–6s
  3) Bodyweight squat 3x10, 2011
  4) Glute bridge 3x12
  5) Hollow hold 3x20s
- Session B
  1) Push-up 3x6–8
  2) Row 3x8–10
  3) Split squat 3x8/leg
  4) Hamstring sliders 3x6
  5) Side plank 3x20–30s/side
- Micros: Off or very light mobility/hangs.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Intensification)
Goal: Increase intensity via leverage (feet-elevated), slower eccentrics, and move toward unassisted pull-ups. Rest 90–150s for primary lifts.

Progression notes for pull-ups
- Use these in Sessions A: Start with 3–5 sets of controlled eccentrics (8–10s) immediately after 2–4 assisted reps. Over weeks, reduce leg assist, aim for first clean bodyweight reps by Week 7–8. Use GTG singles on off days.

Week 5
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up (8–16 in elevation) 4x6–8, 31X1
  2) Pull-up cluster: Assisted reps 3x3–5 + 2–3 single eccentrics 8–10s
  3) Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on couch) 4x8/leg, 31X1
  4) Hip thrust feet on couch, single-leg 3x8–10/leg
  5) Hollow body (one leg extended) 4x25–35s
- Session B
  1) Diamond or close-grip push-up 4x8–10, 2111
  2) Horizontal row (towel/inverted) with feet further out 4x8–10, 2112
  3) Tempo squat 4x12, 31X1; last reps 2s pause
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x10
  5) RKC plank 4x15–20s
- Micros: 5–8 sets easy assisted pull-up singles; 2x20–30s active hang.

Week 6
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–8; add backpack load if >8 easy
  2) Pull-up: 4–5 sets 2–3 assisted reps + 2 eccentrics 8–10s; end with scapular pull-ups 2x8
  3) Bulgarian split squat 4x8–10/leg; finish set with 10s iso hold
  4) Single-leg hip thrust 3x10–12/leg
  5) Hollow rock (one leg extended) 4x15–20
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up (hips high) 4x6–8, 31X1
  2) Row 4x10–12 with 2s top hold
  3) Reverse lunge 4x10/leg, 2111
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x10–12
  5) Side plank with reach-through 3x25–30s/side
- Micros: GTG assisted pull-up singles 6–10 total; shoulder mobility.

Week 7
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–9, 31X1
  2) Pull-up: Test singles. Aim 1–3 unassisted singles, then 3x2–3 assisted + 2 eccentrics
  3) Bulgarian split squat 4x10/leg
  4) Hip hinge: Good-morning pattern drill + hamstring sliders 3x12
  5) Hollow body full progression attempts 4x20–30s
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up 4x7–9
  2) Row 4x8–10 feet further forward or add backpack on chest
  3) Tempo squat 4x10, 31X1
  4) Glute bridge march 3x12/side
  5) RKC plank 5x15–20s
- Micros: Active hangs 3x30–40s, easy pull-up singles if fresh.

Week 8 (reload/technique)
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up 3x6–8, 2111
  2) Pull-up practice: 4–5x2 assisted + 2–3 eccentrics 6–8s
  3) Bulgarian split squat 3x8/leg
  4) Hamstring sliders 3x8
  5) Hollow hold 3x20–25s
- Session B
  1) Push-up 3x8–10
  2) Row 3x8–10
  3) Squat 3x10
  4) Glute bridge 3x12
  5) Side plank 3x20–30s
- Micros: Off or light mobility.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation & Performance)
Goal: Solidify full pull-ups, increase push strength, emphasize unilateral legs and core stiffness. Introduce density work and EMOMs while keeping form pristine.

Week 9
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated or weighted backpack push-up 5x5–7, 31X1
  2) Pull-up ladder: Do 6–8 total reps as singles/doubles across sets with perfect form; then 2 eccentrics 8–10s
  3) Bulgarian split squat 5x8/leg with 2s bottom pause
  4) Single-leg hip thrust 4x10/leg
  5) Hollow body hold 4x30–40s
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up 5x5–7
  2) Row 5x6–8 with 3s top hold or archer row variation
  3) Tempo squat 4x12, 31X1
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x10–12
  5) Hanging knee raise or tuck raise from bar 4x6–10 (slow)
- Micros: 10–12 total easy pull-up singles through the week, active hangs.

Week 10
- Session A
  1) Push-up density: 10-minute EMOM 5–7 feet-elevated reps (quality-first); total 50–70 reps
  2) Pull-ups 6–10 total reps as singles/doubles; add assisted reps to reach 15 total vertical pulls
  3) Bulgarian split squat 4x10/leg; last set AMRAP-1
  4) Hollow rock 4x20–30
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up 5x6–8 or elevated pike for more load
  2) Row 4x8–10 with backpack load if needed
  3) Cossack squat (assisted holding doorframe) 3x6–8/side
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x12
  5) RKC plank 5x20s
- Micros: Shoulder prehab (wall slides, Y-T-W) 2x/week 10 min.

Week 11
- Session A
  1) Weighted backpack push-up or higher feet elevation 5x5–6, 31X1
  2) Pull-ups 8–12 total reps; cluster 1-1-1 with 20–30s between; then 1–2 eccentrics
  3) Bulgarian split squat 5x8/leg, 31X1; iso hold 10s after last set
  4) Hanging knee raise 4x8–10
  5) Side plank 3x30–40s/side
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up 5x6–8
  2) Row 5x6–8 with 2–3s top hold
  3) Shrimp squat (assisted holding doorframe) 4x4–6/leg, 31X1
  4) Hamstring sliders 4x10–12
  5) Hollow body hold 4x30–40s
- Micros: Easy pull-up singles if fresh; mobility.

Week 12 (test week)
- Session A (Test upper push/pull)
  1) Push-up test: Max strict reps (chest-to-floor, no hips sag) or max at feet-elevated height used in Week 9; stop at form break.
  2) Pull-up test: Max strict singles with full hang, chin over bar; rest ~60–90s between attempts. If still assisted, test max 5–8s controlled eccentrics count (how many quality eccentrics).
  3) Accessories easy: Bulgarian split squat 2x8/leg, hollow hold 2x20s.
- Session B (Lower + core focus)
  1) Bulgarian split squat 4x10/leg
  2) Hamstring sliders 4x10–12
  3) Hanging knee raises 4x8–10 slow
  4) Pike push-up 3x6–8 easy
- Micros: Light mobility only.

Technique and safety notes
- Doorway pull-up bar: Ensure proper installation per manufacturer; test with low, controlled load first. Use a stable chair for foot-assisted reps.
- Wrists/shoulders: Keep wrists neutral on push-ups; externally rotate shoulders slightly, pack scapulae on pulls.
- Core bracing: Ribcage down, glutes lightly engaged during pushes/pulls to avoid overextension.

Progression rules
- If you hit the top of the rep range on all sets with perfect form, progress next session by: harder variation, small backpack load, or slower tempo/longer pause.
- If fewer than target reps, repeat same prescription next session; if stuck 2+ sessions, slightly regress leverage or add rest.
- Aim RPE 8–9 on last working set for main lifts; accessories RPE 7–8.

Optional conditioning (2x/week on non-lifting days, 10–20 min)
- Low-impact circuits: 3–5 rounds of 30s brisk step-ups on a stable step, 30s marching with high knees, 30s bear crawl or plank shoulder taps, 30–60s rest.
- Keep easy/moderate; do not compromise recovery for strength sessions.

Recovery, mobility, and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly; consistent schedule.
- Walk daily: 20–30 minutes if possible.
- Post-session cooldown: 3–5 minutes breathing (nasal inhales, long exhales), gentle hip flexor and pec doorway stretches 60–90s.
- Soreness management: Light mobility, walking, and easy GTG hangs.

Nutrition basics for strength and recovery
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily, evenly across 3–5 meals.
- Calories: Slight surplus (+150–300 kcal) if gaining strength/size is a goal; at least maintenance if body comp is unknown.
- Carbs: Anchor around training (pre and post) for energy and recovery.
- Hydration: ~30–35 ml/kg/day water as a baseline; add more with sweat.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time; safe for most healthy adults.
- Pre-workout meal: 60–120 min before, include carbs + protein (e.g., yogurt + fruit, oats + whey).
- Post-workout: 20–40 g protein within a few hours; include carbs.

How to coach remotely
- Request short form-check videos: push-up side view, pull-up front view, squat front/side, split squat front.
- Use RPE notes and rep quality to adjust: reduce volume if technique degrades; add sets if easy.
- Weekly check-in metrics: session completion, best pull-up variation achieved, max quality push-ups, unilateral leg symmetry notes, soreness (0–10), sleep hours.

Expected outcomes by Week 12
- Push: From incline to solid regular or feet-elevated push-ups with higher total volume.
- Pull: From chair-assisted and eccentrics to several clean bodyweight pull-up singles or strong path toward them.
- Legs: Confident with Bulgarian split squats and good depth, improved knee/hip control.
- Core/scapula: Stronger hollow holds, stable shoulder girdle, better posture and hang tolerance.

Here’s a simple, coachable 12-week nutrition plan to support strength gains, recovery, and habit-building. It prioritizes enough protein, steady calories, and easy meal structures a beginner can follow without a full kitchen setup. Adjust portions weekly based on check-ins.

Goals
- Fuel strength: Eat at maintenance to slight surplus (+150–300 kcal/day) to support muscle and skill progress.
- Hit protein: 1.8–2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily, split over 3–5 eating occasions.
- Simple, repeatable meals: Emphasize minimally processed proteins, carbs around training, and fruits/veg.
- Hydration and micronutrients: Keep water and fiber consistent to aid performance and recovery.

Step 1: Establish calories and macros
- If you know his weight, set targets:
  - Calories: Maintenance or +200 kcal if body fat is moderate (waist-to-height ratio <0.53). If higher, start at maintenance.
  - Protein: 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day.
  - Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day.
  - Carbs: Fill remaining calories, bias around training window.
- If weight is unknown, use this quick-start:
  - Men 60–75 kg: 2,200–2,600 kcal/day
  - Men 75–90 kg: 2,600–3,000 kcal/day
  - Men 90–105 kg: 3,000–3,400 kcal/day
  - Then fine-tune by scale trend: aim +0.1–0.25% bodyweight/week. If gaining faster, reduce 150–200 kcal; if flat and strength stalls, add 150–200 kcal.

Macro distribution (example starting point)
- Protein: 30–35% of calories
- Fat: 25–30%
- Carbs: 35–45% (higher on training days)

Meal timing
- 3–4 main meals + 1 snack works well.
- Pre-workout (60–120 min): 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein.
- Post-workout (0–3 h): 30–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs.
- Even protein at each meal (0.4–0.6 g/kg per meal) improves muscle protein synthesis.

12-week habit progression
- Weeks 1–2: Hit protein and hydration.
  - Target: Protein at goal 6/7 days; 8–10 cups water/day; 5+ servings fruit/veg/day.
  - Track simply: tick-box compliance, not full calories.
- Weeks 3–4: Add structure around training.
  - Consistent pre/post-workout meals; 80% of meals from whole foods.
- Weeks 5–6: Portion calibration.
  - Use a hand-portion guide on days you don’t track:
    - Men (per meal): 2 palms protein, 2 cupped hands carbs (1 on rest days), 1–2 thumbs fats, 2 fists veg.
- Weeks 7–8: Refine carbs for performance.
  - Training days: +1 cupped hand carbs at pre/post meals; rest days: -1 cupped hand carbs at two meals.
- Weeks 9–10: Fiber and micronutrients.
  - 25–35 g fiber/day; include a variety of colors daily; salt food to taste, especially if sweating.
- Weeks 11–12: Consistency and auto-regulation.
  - Keep protein, hydration, and pre/post meals rock-solid; adjust carbs by appetite and session difficulty.

Simple meal templates (no fancy equipment)
- Protein options (20–40 g per serving):
  - Greek yogurt or skyr; cottage cheese; eggs/egg whites; canned tuna/salmon/mackerel; rotisserie chicken; lean deli meats; tofu/tempeh/edamame; whey/plant protein shakes.
- Carb options (40–80 g per serving):
  - Oats; rice/microwave rice; wholegrain bread/wraps; potatoes/microwaveable; fruit (bananas, berries, apples, dates); pasta; lentils/beans (canned).
- Fat options (10–20 g per serving):
  - Olive oil, avocado, nuts/nut butter, seeds, full-fat dairy, dark chocolate.
- Veggies:
  - Microwave-steam bags, pre-washed salads, jarred roasted peppers, baby carrots, cherry tomatoes, frozen mixes.

Sample day (training day, ~2,700 kcal; adjust portions)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt bowl (300 g) + oats (60 g) + berries + 1 tbsp peanut butter.
- Lunch: Wraps x2 with chicken (160 g), mixed salad, hummus; side fruit.
- Pre-workout snack (~90 min): Banana + whey shake (30–35 g protein) in water or milk.
- Post-workout meal: Microwave rice (250 g cooked) + canned salmon (150 g drained) + microwave veg + olive oil drizzle.
- Evening: Eggs (3) + egg whites (150 ml) scramble with spinach and cheese; wholegrain toast.

Sample day (rest day, ~2,400 kcal)
- Breakfast: Omelette (3 eggs) + toast + fruit.
- Lunch: Lentil/bean salad bowl with feta, olive oil, lots of veg.
- Snack: Skyr (250 g) + nuts (20–30 g).
- Dinner: Tofu stir-fry (pan or microwave-steam veg + tofu) over rice; smaller carb portion than training day.

Supplements (optional, evidence-based)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily; no loading needed. Expect 1–2 kg water-weight increase early; supports strength.
- Vitamin D3: 1,000–2,000 IU/day if low sun exposure or as per bloodwork.
- Fish oil: 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if fatty fish <2x/week.
- Whey/plant protein: Convenience to hit targets.
- Caffeine: 1–3 mg/kg 30–60 min pre-workout if desired and tolerated.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Baseline water: 30–35 ml/kg/day.
- Add 500–750 ml around workouts.
- Salt meals to taste; if cramping or very sweaty, add a pinch of salt to pre-workout water.

Alcohol and extras
- Limit to ≤4 drinks/week; avoid within 3–4 hours pre-bed and on heavy training days.
- Keep 80–90% of intake nutrient-dense; leave 10–20% calories for flexibility.

Monitoring and adjustments (weekly check-in)
- Metrics: Morning bodyweight (3–4x/week average), performance notes, appetite, sleep, digestion.
- Targets:
  - Weight: +0.1–0.25%/week. If >0.4%/week for 2 weeks, reduce 150–200 kcal. If <0.05%/week for 2 weeks and lifts aren’t improving, add 150–200 kcal.
  - Protein: ≥90% of days at target.
  - Fruit/veg: 5+ servings/day on 5+ days/week.
  - Sleep: 7–9 hours.
- Biofeedback red flags: Persistent low energy, poor recovery, disrupted sleep, or GI issues—adjust meal size/timing, fiber types, and caffeine.

Special considerations for a small flat and busy schedule
- Batch-shop: Stock microwave grains, frozen veg, canned proteins, yogurt/skyr, eggs, fruit, nuts, olive oil.
- 10-minute prep rule: Build meals that assemble in 10 minutes or less.
- Keep a default “busy day” plan: Shake + banana; wraps with pre-cooked protein; microwave rice + canned fish + veg.

Here’s a simple, progressive 12‑week at‑home cardio plan that complements the strength program, needs no extra equipment, and respects neighbors. It uses low‑impact options, short intervals, and steady work to build aerobic base and conditioning without compromising strength gains.

Guidelines
- Frequency: 2 sessions/week to start; progress to 3/week by Phase 3 if recovery is good.
- Duration: 15–30 minutes per session.
- Intensity anchors:
  - Easy (Zone 2): Conversational pace, RPE 3–4/10, 60–70% max HR.
  - Moderate: RPE 5–6.
  - Hard intervals: RPE 7–8; you should need the recovery period.
- Surfaces/noise: Favor marching, step-ups, shadowboxing, low-impact circuits. If jumping is okay, you can add low‑amplitude hops later.
- Do cardio on non-lifting days or after strength sessions. Keep at least 6–8 hours apart from hard strength if possible.
- Warm-up (every session, 4–5 min): March in place → arm circles → hip circles → ankle rocks → 2x 20s brisk march + 20s easy.

Approved at-home modalities
- Brisk march in place or around the flat
- Step-ups on a stable chair/step (height ~30–45 cm)
- Shadowboxing with light footwork
- Low-impact “aerobic flow” circuits: alternating movements continuously
- Stationary cycling (if he has access later), jump rope (optional, low volume if neighbors allow)
- Bear crawl, plank shoulder taps, mountain climbers (controlled), mini lateral shuffles

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Build aerobic base and movement skill
- Goal: 2x/week, 15–20 min/session, mostly easy to moderate.

Week 1–2 (choose one option per session)
- Option A: Steady easy
  - 15–20 min continuous: brisk march + shadowboxing rounds (1 min march, 1 min shadowbox, repeat).
- Option B: Low-impact intervals
  - 6–8 rounds: 45s moderate step-ups (alternate legs every rep) + 45s easy march. Total 18–24 min.
- Option C: Aerobic flow circuit
  - 3–4 rounds, continuous with minimal rest (4–5 min/round):
    - 1 min march in place
    - 30s step-ups (switch lead halfway)
    - 30s shadowboxing
    - 30s bear crawl forward/back (slow, quiet) or plank shoulder taps
    - 30s lateral shuffle or side step
  - Cooldown 2–3 min easy march + nasal breathing.

Week 3–4
- Progress either volume or slight intensity:
  - Steady easy: 20–25 min continuous.
  - Intervals: 8–10 rounds of 45s moderate work + 30–45s easy.
  - Aerobic flow: 4–5 rounds (20–25 min total).
- Optional short finisher after one strength day: 6 min EMOM
  - Odd minutes: 30s step-ups, 30s easy march
  - Even minutes: 30s shadowboxing, 30s easy march

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Introduce structured intervals; maintain one easy session
- Goal: 2–3x/week, 18–28 min. Keep one true Zone 2 session for recovery.

Weekly structure example
- Session 1 (Zone 2): 22–26 min continuous brisk march + shadowboxing (2:1 ratio).
- Session 2 (Tempo intervals): 8–10 rounds of 40s hard (RPE 7–8) + 50–60s easy.
  - Hard block options: fast step-ups, fast march with high knees (quiet), shadowbox flurries, controlled mountain climbers.
- Optional Session 3 (if recovery solid): Threshold ladder
  - 3 sets of: 2 min moderate-hard + 2 min easy; 3 min moderate-hard + 2 min easy; 2 min moderate-hard + 2 min easy. Total ~23 min.

Progression notes
- Increase rounds or extend hard intervals by 5–10s each week if RPE stays ≤8 and strength training isn’t compromised.
- If legs feel beat up, swap hard step-ups for upper-body-dominant shadowboxing intervals.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate aerobic fitness; add density without soreness
- Goal: 3x/week if recovery allows; otherwise maintain 2x/week. 20–30 min/session.

Weekly structure example
- Session 1 (Zone 2 anchor): 25–30 min continuous easy-moderate.
- Session 2 (VO2-lite intervals): 10 rounds of 30s hard + 60s easy, or 8 rounds of 40s hard + 60–75s easy.
- Session 3 (Mixed density EMOM, 20 min):
  - Minute 1: 40s step-ups (steady)
  - Minute 2: 40s shadowboxing flurries
  - Minute 3: 40s march/high knees (quiet)
  - Minute 4: 40s mobility flow (world’s greatest stretch variations)
  - Repeat x5 cycles; keep breathing nasally if possible to regulate intensity.

Noise-friendly alternatives
- If neighbors complain, prioritize:
  - Long Zone 2 marches, shadowboxing without stomping, slow mountain climbers, step-ups with controlled descent, isometric “cardio” blocks (long bear crawl holds with slow steps), mini-band walks if a band is later added.

Easy on-ramp and deload alignment
- Deload on Weeks 4 and 8 with lower volume (cut intervals/rounds by ~30–40%).
- If a strength session felt very tough, make the next cardio session Zone 2 only.

RPE guide and checks
- Finish cardio feeling like you could do 5–10 more minutes.
- If morning resting heart rate jumps >8–10 bpm above normal or legs feel heavy for 2+ days, reduce intensity/volume by 20–30% that week.

Optional indoor “hike” for variety (if a staircase is accessible and safe)
- 15–25 minutes of steady stair climbing at conversational pace. Descend slowly to protect knees; keep it quiet.

Cool-down (2–3 min)
- Easy march, then 3–5 slow nasal breaths, 30–45s calf, hip flexor, and pec doorway stretches.

Fueling notes for cardio days
- Keep protein target unchanged.
- For sessions ≥25 min with intervals, add a small carb snack pre (fruit or 1 cupped hand carbs).
- Hydrate: 300–500 ml water during or right after.

This cardio plan builds a robust aerobic base, supports recovery between strength sets, and improves work capacity without requiring equipment or compromising the 12-week strength progression.

Great question. For a small flat and a bodyweight-focused plan, add compact, versatile pieces that meaningfully expand loading options without taking much space or damaging floors. Prioritize in this order based on budget.

Tier 1 (immediate impact, minimal space)
- Resistance bands set (light to heavy, with door anchor): For rows, assisted pull-ups, push-up loading, hip work, face pulls, banded RDLs, warm-ups. Cheap, portable, huge versatility.
- Gymnastic rings or suspension trainer (hang from pull-up bar): Enables ring rows at adjustable angles, dips (if ceiling height allows), face pulls, fallouts/ab rollouts, Bulgarian split squat support. Packs into a small bag.
- Weighted backpack or dip belt substitute: Load with books/water jugs for push-ups, squats, hip thrusts, and to add load to pull-ups once he’s ready.

Tier 2 (small footprint, big strength return)
- Adjustable dumbbells (spin-lock or quick-change, target up to 2x20–25 kg per hand eventually; start with 2x10–15 kg if budget-limited): Unlocks heavy unilateral leg work, dumbbell presses/rows, RDLs, push press, floor press. Choose flat-edged plates to avoid rolling; use floor-protecting mat.
- Adjustable kettlebell (8–24 kg or 12–32 kg adjustable): Excellent for swings, goblet squats, cleans, presses, snatches, single-leg RDLs. If only one bell, pick 16–20 kg to start for general strength; progress to 24 kg as he advances. Adjustable saves space.
- Ab wheel (or use rings for fallouts): Tiny, great for anterior core strength.

Tier 3 (if space/budget allow, still apartment-friendly)
- Foldable adjustable bench (flat-to-incline): Pairs with DBs for presses, rows, hip thrust setup.
- Loadable dumbbell handles + plates (standard or Olympic): More cost-effective long-term than fixed DBs and share plates with a future barbell.
- Weight plates set (e.g., pair of 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10 kg): Micro-loading and versatility with DB handles or a dip belt for weighted pull-ups.
- Doorway/portable dip bars or a stable parallettes set: For dips, L-sit work, rows, deficit push-ups. Ensure rubber feet for noise.

Nice-to-have accessories
- Yoga blocks and sliders: For hamstring curls, core variations, elevated hands, mobility.
- Lifting straps: Helpful for high-rep rows/RDLs without frying grip.
- Hip circle/minibands: Glute activation and knee tracking.
- Floor-protecting mat: Noise control and to protect floors under DBs/kettlebell.

What to buy first (practical paths)
- Budget minimal (~£50–100): Bands + rings/suspension trainer + ab wheel. Immediate upgrade to pulling and core; takes a drawer of space.
- Mid-range (~£150–300): Add adjustable dumbbells to the above. Most exercises now loadable; biggest bang for buck.
- Higher budget (~£300–600): Adjustable DBs to 25 kg each or loadable handles + plate set, adjustable kettlebell, foldable bench. This setup covers full-body progressive strength for years.

Safety and apartment tips
- Always check doorway bar and ring anchors; use rated hardware only.
- Keep a thick mat under weights to absorb noise and protect floors.
- Control eccentrics—no dropping DBs or bells.
- Store plates/DBs vertically against a wall or under a bed to save space.

With bands and rings alone he’ll massively expand pull and core options; adding adjustable dumbbells brings true progressive overload to every movement pattern while staying small-flat friendly.

Got it. Here’s how to turn Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) into a higher-intensity block while staying safe in a small flat. We’ll push harder via: lower rep targets, more challenging leverage, cluster sets, slower eccentrics/longer pauses, and strategic density work. Rest 2–3 minutes on primary push/pull/leg moves. Keep Week 8 as a reload but still higher than before.

Global rules for Phase 2 (applies Weeks 5–8)
- Primary lifts intensity: Aim RPE 8–9 on final set; top sets 4–6 reps most days.
- Rep schemes: Use top set + back-off, clusters, and EMOMs for volume.
- Tempos/pauses: 4–5s eccentrics on key sets; 2–3s pauses at bottom on push-ups and Bulgarians.
- Pull-up path: Every session starts with max-quality singles/doubles before any assistance; finish with 1–2 long eccentrics.
- Lower volume accessories: Keep but trim sets to avoid fatigue bleed.
- Micro-sessions: 2x/week grease-the-groove pull-ups (very low RPE), 1 short push-up density block.

Week 5 (Intensification kick-off)
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up (add backpack if needed) Top set 6RM, then 2 back-off sets at −10% reps x6 with 41X1 tempo.
  2) Pull-ups: Ladder singles/doubles up to 6–8 total strict reps. Then 2x1 eccentric 8–10s.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 4x6–8/leg with 3s bottom pause, heavy RPE 8–9.
  4) Single-leg hip thrust: 3x8–10/leg, 21X1.
  5) Hollow body hold: 4x30–35s.
- Session B
  1) Pike push-up (hips high; elevate feet if strong): Top set 5–6 reps @ RPE 9; then 3x4–5 @ 31X1.
  2) Row (towel/inverted): 5x6–8 with 2–3s top hold (hard angle or backpack).
  3) Tempo squat: 4x8–10 @ 31X1, last rep 3s pause.
  4) Hamstring sliders: 3x10–12.
  5) RKC plank: 4x20s.

Micros: One day 8–10 minutes push-up EMOM 5 reps (hard variation), plus 6–8 total easy pull-up singles across two days.

Week 6 (Clusters and longer eccentrics)
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated/weighted push-up cluster: 4 clusters of 2-2-2 (6 total reps/cluster) with 20–30s intra-cluster rest; 2–3 min between clusters. Tempo 41X1 on first rep of each mini-set.
  2) Pull-ups: 5–7 strict singles; if fewer available, fill to 10 total reps with minimal-assist doubles. Finish 2x8–10s eccentrics.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 5x6/leg @ 31X1; 10s iso hold after last rep each set.
  4) Single-leg RDL pattern via sliders/hip hinge: 3x10/leg, slow lower.
  5) Hollow rock (one leg extended): 4x20.

- Session B
  1) Elevated pike push-up (or pseudo planche lean push-up if wrists tolerate): 5x4–6 @ RPE 8–9.
  2) Row heavy: 5x6–8 (add backpack or move feet forward); 3s eccentric.
  3) Reverse lunge: 4x8/leg with 2s pause.
  4) Hamstring sliders: 4x10–12.
  5) Side plank reach-through: 3x30s/side.

Micros: GTG pull-up singles 6–10 total for the week; 6-minute push-up density finisher once (EMOM 6, 4–6 hard reps).

Week 7 (Peak intensity)
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated/weighted push-up heavy day: 6x4–5 @ RPE 9, 41X1 tempo.
  2) Pull-ups: Attempt 1–3 strict singles, then 4x2 cluster (1-1 with 20s rest) assisted as needed. Finish 1–2 eccentrics 10s.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 5x6–8/leg with 3s pause; last set AMRAP-1 (stop 1 rep short of failure).
  4) Single-leg hip thrust: 3x10/leg.
  5) Hollow body hold: 4x35–40s.

- Session B
  1) Pike push-up heavy: 6x4–5 @ RPE 9; if too easy, elevate feet on couch.
  2) Row: 6x5–6 super-strict with 3s top hold; final set AMRAP-1.
  3) Tempo squat: 4x8 @ 31X1.
  4) Hamstring sliders: 4x12.
  5) Hanging knee raise or tuck raise: 4x6–8 slow.

Micros: Optional only if recovering well: 8–10 total easy pull-up singles; skip push-up finisher this week if joints feel beat up.

Week 8 (Reload but still purposeful)
- Session A
  1) Feet-elevated push-up: 3x5–6 @ RPE ~7, 3111.
  2) Pull-ups: 5x1–2 technique reps (strict), then 1 eccentric 8s.
  3) Bulgarian split squat: 3x6–8/leg, controlled.
  4) Hamstring sliders: 3x10.
  5) Hollow hold: 3x25–30s.

- Session B
  1) Pike push-up: 3x4–6 smooth.
  2) Row: 3x8 easy angle.
  3) Squat: 3x8–10 easy.
  4) Glute bridge: 3x12.
  5) Side plank: 3x20–30s/side.

Additional intensity tactics you can deploy
- Mechanical drop sets on push-ups: Start feet-elevated to near-failure, immediately drop to regular push-ups, then to incline. Use sparingly (1 set, Week 6 or 7).
- Extended eccentrics: On last set of push-ups or rows, perform a 10s lower on each of the last 2–3 reps.
- Partial-ROM overload: For pull-ups, add 2–3 top-half partials after your last single to build overbar strength.

Recovery safeguards
- Keep elbows at ~45° on push-ups, pack shoulders on pulls; maintain bracing.
- If elbow/shoulder niggles appear, reduce density work first, then clusters; keep strict singles only.
- Sleep 7–9 hours, protein 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day, carbs up around hard sessions.
- Deload adherence in Week 8—don’t skip it.

Here’s a fun, apartment-friendly Saturday “Finisher Day” that feels like play but still builds conditioning, core, and skill. It’s modular: pick one theme each Saturday and rotate. Each takes 20–30 minutes including warm-up and cooldown. Keep intensity high but form crisp; stop sets 1–2 reps before technique breaks.

General structure
- Warm-up (5 min): March in place 1 min → arm circles 30s → hip circles 30s → inchworms x5 → scap pull-ups x6 or active hang 20s → 20s brisk march + 20s easy x2.
- Choose one theme below.
- Cooldown (3 min): Easy march + 3–5 slow nasal breaths + light pec/hip flexor stretch.

Theme 1: Pull-up Party + Core Carnival
- Ladder + game format
1) Pull-up/supported pull-up ladder 1–2–3–2–1
   - Do unassisted singles if possible; otherwise use light leg assist or band. Rest ~45–60s between rungs.
2) Hanging core medley x3 rounds
   - 6–10 hanging knee raises (controlled 2s up/2s down)
   - 15–20s active hang
   - 20s hollow body hold on mat
   - Rest 60–90s
3) Beat-the-clock finisher (6 min EMOM)
   - Minute 1: 4–6 strict pull-up reps total as singles/doubles (assisted as needed)
   - Minute 2: 20–30s plank shoulder taps (slow, quiet) + 20–30s easy march

Theme 2: Push-up Gauntlet + Rings/Bar Skill
- Mechanical drop set play x3 rounds, rest 2–3 min between
  - A: Feet-elevated push-ups AMRAP-2 (stop 2 reps shy of failure)
  - Drop to: Regular push-ups AMRAP-2
  - Drop to: Incline push-ups (hands on couch/counter) AMRAP-2
- Skill block (8 min every-2-minutes-on-the-minute, E2MOM)
  - Odd rounds: Support hold top of pull-up bar or rings 20–30s (scaps down/back) + 10 slow scap pull-ups
  - Even rounds: Ring/RTR rows 8–10 with 2s top hold, or towel rows if no rings
- Core closer
  - Hollow rocks 3x15–20, 45–60s rest

Theme 3: Lower-Body Burner (quiet, no jumping)
- Triplet circuit x4–5 rounds (work steady, minimal rest, 12–15 min)
  - Bulgarian split squat 8/leg, 2s pause bottom
  - Hamstring sliders 10–12 controlled
  - Lateral step-backs/side lunges 8/side (hold doorframe for balance)
- Finisher game: 5-minute continuous “stairs without stairs”
  - 20s high-knee march (quiet) + 10 step-ups each leg on sturdy chair/low step; repeat continuously at conversational pace

Theme 4: Shadowbox + Steps Sweat
- Rounds: 8 x 2 minutes on, 1 minute easy
  - Work blocks alternate:
    - Round 1,3,5,7: Shadowboxing with light footwork, 10s flurries every 40s
    - Round 2,4,6,8: Step-ups steady pace, switch lead every 10 reps
  - Keep RPE ~7 on work blocks
- Core wrap: Side plank 2x30–40s/side + dead bug 2x10/side

Theme 5: EMOM Mixer (20 minutes)
- Minute 1: Pull-ups 1–3 strict or 3–5 assisted, then active hang to 30s total
- Minute 2: Push-ups 8–12 (feet-elevated if strong)
- Minute 3: Step-ups 20–30 total reps
- Minute 4: Hollow hold 30–40s + 10–12 slow mountain climbers
- Scale reps to finish each minute in 40–45s. Keep last 15–20s as rest.

Theme 6: “Choose Your Quest” Scorekeeper
- 15-minute AMRAP (as many quality rounds as possible)
  - 3 pull-ups (assisted if needed)
  - 6 push-ups (variation you can keep perfect)
  - 9 squats (2s down, 1s pause)
  - 20s hollow hold
- Record rounds + reps; aim to beat your score next time with same variations.

Monthly rotation idea
- Week 1: EMOM Mixer
- Week 2: Pull-up Party + Core
- Week 3: Shadowbox + Steps
- Week 4: Push-up Gauntlet
- Repeat, swapping Lower-Body Burner for any week if legs feel fresh.

Rules to keep it “fun” and safe
- Music on, strict form. No failure—leave 1–2 reps in the tank.
- Scale instantly: reduce elevation, use assistance, or cut reps to keep flow.
- If elbows/shoulders feel cranky, substitute more rows/hangs and fewer dips/gauntlet sets that day.
- Keep Sunday light (walk and mobility) to start the week recovered.

Fuel/hydrate
- Small carb + protein snack 60–90 minutes before if training hard (banana + yogurt or whey).
- 300–500 ml water during/after.

These Saturday finishers add variety, a little competition, and extra calorie burn without wrecking recovery for the main program. Pick what he enjoys most and chase small weekly PRs in quality and flow.

Here’s a simple, repeatable mobility routine he can do in 12–15 minutes on rest days or after sessions. It targets spine, shoulders/scapula, hips, ankles, and hamstrings—common limiters for pull-ups, push-ups, and split squats. Use slow breathing and control. No equipment beyond the mat and doorway bar.

How to use
- Frequency: 4–6 days/week (post-workout 8–10 min; on rest days 12–15 min).
- Tempo: 3–4 slow breaths per position; move smoothly, no bouncing.
- Breathing: Inhale through nose, long relaxed exhale (1.5–2x inhale length). Keep ribs down, light core brace.

Daily mobility flow (12–15 minutes)
1) Reset and breathe (1 minute)
- Crocodile breathing: Lie prone, forehead on hands. 6–8 slow breaths, feel belly/ribs expand into the floor.

2) Thoracic spine + shoulders (2–3 minutes)
- Cat–cow x6 slow reps.
- Thread the needle: 2x3–4 reps/side with 2–3s pause at end range.
- Wall angels or floor “snow angels” x6–8 reps, ribs down.

3) Scapular control and hanging (2–3 minutes)
- Scapular pull-ups: Hang from the bar (or partial weight with toes on floor). 2x6–8 reps: depress and retract shoulder blades, then return to full hang.
- Active hang hold: 2x20–30s focusing on long spine, shoulders down and back. If a full hang is too intense, bend knees and keep toes light on the floor.

4) Hips front/back (3 minutes)
- Hip flexor half-kneeling stretch: 2x30–40s/side, glute of the back leg engaged; light posterior pelvic tilt.
- 90/90 hip rotations: 6–8 controlled switches, pause 1–2s upright in each position. If tight, use hands for support.

5) Hamstrings + posterior chain (2 minutes)
- Supine hamstring stretch with strap/towel: 2x30–40s/side, keep knee soft, ankle dorsiflexed.
- Glute figure-4 stretch: 1x30–40s/side, keep pelvis level.

6) Adductors + lateral hip (1–2 minutes)
- Rocking adductor stretch (half-kneel with extended leg to side): 8–10 slow rocks/side, then 20–30s hold/side.

7) Ankles + calves (1–2 minutes)
- Knee-to-wall ankle rocks: 2x10–12 reps/side with heel down; hold last rep 20–30s.
- Standing calf stretch on wall or step: 1x20–30s/side.

8) Shoulder extension and pecs (1–2 minutes)
- Doorway pec stretch (low-to-mid angle): 2x20–30s/side; keep ribs down.
- Table/couch shoulder extension stretch: Hands behind on couch, fingers forward, slide hips forward slightly, open chest, 20–30s hold x1–2.

Optional add-ons (rotate as needed, 2–3 minutes total)
- Cossack squat pulses: 6–8 reps/side for lateral hip/ankle.
- Jefferson curl patterning (no load or very light backpack): 2x5 super-slow, segmental spinal flexion to comfortable range.
- Ring/Bar lat stretch: From hang, side-bend gently, 20–30s/side.

Mini pre-lift warm-up (5–7 minutes) if he wants a quick version
- 30s march + 10 arm circles each way
- Cat–cow x5
- World’s Greatest Stretch x2/side (lunge with T-spine rotation)
- Scap pull-ups x6 + active hang 20s
- 10 bodyweight squats with 2s pause at bottom
- 20s high plank to fire up core

Post-session cooldown (3–5 minutes)
- Nasal breathing in 90/90 position (on back, feet on couch, knees 90°) x6–8 breaths.
- Hip flexor stretch 30s/side.
- Doorway pec stretch 30s/side.

Weekly structure suggestion
- On strength days: Do the mini warm-up before, and the 3–5 minute cooldown.
- On cardio/finisher/rest days: Do the full 12–15 minute flow.
- If time-crunched: Hit Sections 2, 3, and 4 (T-spine/shoulders, hanging, hips) for a 6–8 minute micro-dose.

Mobility progress markers (check monthly)
- Active hang: comfortable 45–60s total time under tension.
- Ankle dorsiflexion: knee-to-wall distance improves by 1–2 cm.
- Hip 90/90: can sit upright hands-free for 30–40s per side.
- Thoracic rotation: thread-the-needle elbow reaches floor lightly with ribs down.

Tips
- Move within comfort; mild stretch is good, pinching/sharp pain is not.
- Keep consistency over intensity—daily small wins beat occasional long sessions.
- Pair long exhales with the tightest positions to relax guard tension.

This routine keeps shoulders happy for pull-ups, opens hips for deep split squats, and maintains ankles/hamstrings for stable squatting—all from a small flat with zero extra gear.

- Session B: Pike push-up 3x4–6; row 3x8; squat 3x8–10; glute bridge 3x12; side plank 3x20–30s

- Goal: Cement full pull-ups, push strength, unilateral legs; add density tests smartly.

Cardio plan (at home, 2–3x/week, 15–30 min)
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): 2x/week, easy/moderate
  - Options: 15–25 min steady march + shadowbox; or 6–10 rounds 45s step-ups + 30–45s easy; or 4–5 rounds aerobic flow (5 min/round)
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Keep 1 Zone 2 session; add structured intervals
  - Session 1: 22–26 min continuous Zone 2
  - Session 2: 8–10 rounds 40s hard + 50–60s easy (step-ups, fast march, shadowbox)
  - Optional Session 3: Ladder intervals 2–3–2 min moderate-hard with 2 min easy between
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): 2–3x/week
  - Session 1: 25–30 min Zone 2
  - Session 2: 8–10 rounds 30–40s hard + 60–75s easy
  - Session 3: 20-min EMOM mixer (step-ups, shadowboxing, high-knee march, mobility)

Saturday “Fun Finisher” (pick one each week, 20–30 min)
- Pull-up Party + Core: Ladder 1–2–3–2–1; hanging core medley; 6-min EMOM with pull-up singles + plank taps
- Push-up Gauntlet: 3 mechanical drop-set rounds; E2MOM skill block (supports, scap pulls, rows); hollow rocks

- Flow: Crocodile breathing → cat–cow + thread-the-needle → wall/floor angels → scap pulls + active hang → hip flexor half-kneel → 90/90 switches → hamstring strap stretch → adductor rocks → ankle knee-to-wall → doorway pec stretch → shoulder extension on couch
- Mini warm-up pre-lift: March 30s, arm circles, cat–cow x5, World’s Greatest x2/side, scap pulls x6 + active hang 20s, 10 pause squats, 20s plank
- Post-session cooldown: 90/90 breathing, hip flexor and pec stretch

Nutrition plan (12 weeks, habit-based with macros)
- Calories: Maintenance to slight surplus (+150–300 kcal/day) to drive strength; adjust weekly by scale trend (+0.1–0.25% BW/week)
- Protein: 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day (evenly across 3–5 meals)
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; Carbs fill remainder (higher on training days)
- Timing: Pre (60–120 min): 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; Post (0–3 h): 30–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs
- Habits by phase:
  - Weeks 1–2: Nail protein, hydration (8–10 cups), 5+ fruit/veg/day
  - Weeks 3–4: Lock pre/post meals; 80% whole foods
  - Weeks 5–6: Portion guide (per meal): 2 palms protein, 2 cupped carbs (1 on rest days), 1–2 thumbs fats, 2 fists veg
  - Weeks 7–8: Carb periodization—+1 cupped carb pre/post training; −1 on rest meals
  - Weeks 9–10: Fiber 25–35 g/day; colorful variety; salt to taste
  - Weeks 11–12: Consistency; auto-regulate carbs by hunger and training load
- Supplements (optional): Creatine 3–5 g/day; Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU/day (if low sun); Fish oil 1–2 g EPA+DHA if fish <2x/week; whey/plant protein as needed
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + 500–750 ml around workouts

Equipment roadmap (apartment-friendly)
- Tier 1: Resistance bands + door anchor; rings/suspension trainer; weighted backpack
- Tier 2: Adjustable dumbbells (to 20–25 kg each); adjustable kettlebell (16–24 kg); ab wheel
- Tier 3: Foldable bench; loadable DB handles + plates; portable dip bars/parallettes; floor mat

Coaching and progression notes
- Increase difficulty once top reps hit with perfect form: elevate feet, add backpack load, slow tempo, longer pauses, or add a set.
- Target RPE: 8–9 on last set of primaries; 7–8 for accessories. If stuck 2+ sessions, slightly regress leverage or add rest.
- Pull-up pathway: Prioritize singles; use leg-assisted reps and controlled eccentrics; active hangs and scap pulls every week.
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep; walk 20–30 min daily; use mobility flow most days; deload adherence in Weeks 4 and 8; monitor morning HR and soreness.

Expected outcomes by Week 12
- Push: Regular to feet-elevated push-ups for solid sets; improved rep quality and control
- Pull: Several strict singles or strong assisted sets with long eccentrics; better scapular control and hang tolerance
- Legs: Confident Bulgarian split squats, improved depth/control; stronger hamstrings via sliders
- Core/posture: Longer hollow holds, better bracing; improved shoulder mobility
